# Server-side request to a URL from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/ssrf` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A10_2021-Server-Side_Request_Forgery_%28SSRF%29/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Outgoing HTTP requests whose URL is decided by HTTP request data (Jakarta Servlet, Spring MVC,
Jakarta REST): a `java.net.URL` that is opened, the URI of a `java.net.http.HttpRequest`, the URL
of Spring's `RestTemplate`, and the URI or base URL of a `RestClient` or `WebClient`. Request data
after a fixed scheme, host and `/`, or in URI template variables, is not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
The request leaves from the server, inside your network. A client who picks the URL can make the
server call internal services, admin interfaces or the cloud metadata endpoint
(`http://169.254.169.254/`), which may hand out credentials, and read the answers if the server
passes them on.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the URL to fetch comes from the request.

```java
package com.example.preview;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.HttpClient;
import java.net.http.HttpRequest;
import java.net.http.HttpResponse;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class PreviewController {
    private final HttpClient client = HttpClient.newHttpClient();

    @GetMapping("/preview")
    public int preview(@RequestParam String url) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
        HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(url)).build();
        return client.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.discarding()).statusCode();
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the scheme and host are fixed; request data only fills a path segment.

```java
package com.example.preview;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.net.URI;
import java.net.URLEncoder;
import java.net.http.HttpClient;
import java.net.http.HttpRequest;
import java.net.http.HttpResponse;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class PreviewController {
    private final HttpClient client = HttpClient.newHttpClient();

    @GetMapping("/preview")
    public int preview(@RequestParam String id) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
        URI uri = URI.create("https://api.example.com/users/" + URLEncoder.encode(id, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).build();
        return client.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.discarding()).statusCode();
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the scheme and host fixed: a constant base URL followed by `/`, a `RestClient` or
  `WebClient` built with a fixed `baseUrl`, and URI template variables for the request data
  (`restTemplate.getForObject("https://api.example.com/users/{id}", User.class, id)`).
- If the client must choose the server, check the host against an allow-list before the request
  is sent.
- Block private and link-local addresses at the network level as well.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)
- java.net (URL, URLConnection)
- java.net.http (HttpClient)
- Spring RestTemplate, RestClient and WebClient

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Conditions are not evaluated: an allow-list check of the host does not stop the finding (an
  allow-list lookup that yields constants does).
- A fixed origin is recognised when the URL text starts with it and `/`, `?` or `#` follows the
  host before any request data: a literal, a `static final` or Spring `@Value` base followed by such
  a literal, a `"%s/..."` format, `URL` constructors with literals, a `UriComponentsBuilder` chain
  of up to eight calls from such a base, or a relative path given to a client with a fixed base URL.
  A host constant in the middle of the string and `URI.resolve` on a constant URI are not
  recognised.
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source (the Jakarta REST entity parameter, a
  Spring MVC simple-type parameter), except a Spring `HttpEntity` or `RequestEntity` (the
  request body and headers); enum, `List` or `Optional` parameters still count as request data.
- Allow-list lookups are recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of constants and as `valueOf` of an enum
  declared in the same file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

The test file [`rules/java/ssrf/ssrf.java`](../../../rules/java/ssrf/ssrf.java) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
